title: Old Testament journeys
allSummary: Old Testament journeys, c. 2100–445 BC. Abraham, the Exodus, the conquest of Canaan, the exiles and the return. Tap a chip to follow one, or tap a place for what happened there and where to read it. Dates follow conservative chronology; routes are approximate and several sites are debated.
provKey: No ancient borders shown (they changed over these periods)

0.name: Abraham’s journeys
0.sum: Abraham’s journeys (Genesis 11:31–25:10). From Ur up the Euphrates to Haran, then, at God’s call, into Canaan: Shechem, Bethel, a famine stay in Egypt, Hebron, Beersheba and Mount Moriah. Conservative chronology places Abraham’s call around 2091 BC; many scholars date the patriarchs later, around 1900–1700 BC.

1.name: The Exodus
1.sum: The Exodus to the plains of Moab (Exodus 12 to Deuteronomy 34). From Rameses across the sea to Mount Sinai, then to Kadesh-barnea, forty years in the wilderness, around Edom and up to the plains of Moab. Conservative dating places the Exodus around 1446 BC (from 1 Kings 6:1); many scholars prefer around 1260 BC. The route and several sites, including the sea crossing and Mount Sinai, are debated; traditional locations are shown.

2.name: Conquest of Canaan
2.sum: Joshua’s conquest of Canaan (Joshua 1–24). Across the Jordan to Gilgal and Jericho, then Ai and the covenant at Shechem, the southern campaign after the battle for Gibeon, the northern campaign against Hazor, and the dividing of the land at Shiloh. Routes are simplified, and some sites (such as Ai) are debated.

3.name: Exile to Assyria and Babylon
3.sum: The exiles (2 Kings 17; 2 Kings 24–25). Israel’s northern kingdom falls to Assyria in 722 BC and its people are deported to the Habor river and Media. Judah is taken to Babylon in three waves (605, 597 and 586 BC), and Jerusalem and the temple are destroyed. Armies and captives followed the curve of the Fertile Crescent, not a straight line across the desert.

4.name: Return from exile
4.sum: The return (Ezra and Nehemiah). Cyrus’s decree of 538 BC lets the exiles go home. Zerubbabel leads the first return and the temple is rebuilt by 516 BC; Ezra brings a second group in 458 BC; Nehemiah comes from Susa in 445 BC to rebuild Jerusalem’s walls. Some of the people (like Esther’s family) stayed in the east.

0: Abram’s family home. Terah sets out from Ur with Abram, Sarai and Lot, heading for Canaan. God had called Abram here (Acts 7:2–4).
The family settles in Haran, and Terah dies here. At 75, Abram receives God’s call and promise (“I will make of thee a great nation”) and leaves with Sarai, Lot and all their household.
3: Haran is one of the places the Assyrians had conquered (2 Kings 19:12). The Israelite exiles were taken to Gozan on the Habor river, close by.

0: Abram’s chief servant was “Eliezer of Damascus”, and Abram later pursues the kings who took Lot as far as Hobah, north of Damascus. Tradition places his route into Canaan through here.
3: On the main road north. The armies and deportees of Assyria and Babylon passed this way between Israel and Mesopotamia.
4: The returning exiles came home along the same northern road through Syria.

0: Abram’s first stop in Canaan, at the oak of Moreh. The LORD appears to him and promises, “Unto thy seed will I give this land,” and Abram builds an altar.
2: Between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim, near Shechem, Joshua builds an altar and reads the whole law to Israel, as Moses had commanded. Joshua later gathers the tribes here to renew the covenant.

0: Abram camps between Bethel and Ai and builds an altar. He returns here from Egypt, and here he and Lot separate.
Famine drives Abram down to Egypt. Fearing for his life, he says Sarai is his sister, and Pharaoh takes her until the LORD strikes his house with plagues.
Abram settles by the oaks of Mamre at Hebron and builds an altar. Here three visitors promise a son to Sarah. He buys the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah, and he is buried there himself.
2: Joshua takes Hebron in the southern campaign. Later Caleb, aged 85, asks for Hebron as his inheritance and drives out the Anakim.

0: Abraham digs a well and makes a covenant with Abimelech here, plants a tamarisk tree and calls on the name of the LORD. He sets out from here to Moriah and returns here afterwards.

1: Israel had built the store-city of Rameses as slaves. After the tenth plague and the first Passover, about 600,000 men on foot, besides children, set out from Rameses.
Israel’s first camp. God leads them by a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night, not by the shorter road through Philistine country.

redsea.m: Traditional site: northern Gulf of Suez (location debated)

1: Camped by Pi-hahiroth, Israel is trapped between Pharaoh’s army and the sea. Moses stretches out his hand, the waters part, Israel crosses on dry ground, and the waters return over the Egyptians. Where it happened is debated: the Bitter Lakes, the Gulf of Suez and the Gulf of Aqaba have all been proposed.

marah.m: Traditionally Ain Hawara and Wadi Gharandel, Sinai

1: At Marah the water is bitter until Moses throws in a tree and it becomes sweet. At Elim they find twelve springs and seventy palm trees.
In the wilderness of Sin God sends manna and quail. At Rephidim water flows from the rock, and Israel defeats Amalek while Aaron and Hur hold up Moses’ hands.

sinai.m: Traditionally Jebel Musa, Sinai, Egypt (location debated)

1: Israel camps before the mountain for about a year. God gives the Ten Commandments and the law, the covenant is made, the golden calf is judged, and the tabernacle is built. Jebel Musa is the traditional site; others have been proposed in Sinai and in Arabia.
Twelve spies go out from here into Canaan. Ten bring a bad report, the people refuse to go in, and God sentences them to forty years in the wilderness. Miriam dies here, and Moses strikes the rock.

eziongeber.m: Near Aqaba and Eilat, at the Gulf of Aqaba

1: One of the late wilderness camps. Refused passage through Edom, Israel goes south to the Red Sea and around Edom’s land.

hor.m: Traditionally Jebel Harun, near Petra, Jordan

1: On the border of Edom, Aaron dies on Mount Hor and his son Eleazar becomes high priest. Soon after, the bronze serpent is lifted up.
Sihon, king of Heshbon, refuses Israel passage and attacks. Israel defeats him and then Og, king of Bashan, taking the land east of the Jordan.

moab.n: Plains of Moab and Mount Nebo
moab.m: Plains north-east of the Dead Sea; Mount Nebo, Jordan

1: Israel camps on the plains of Moab opposite Jericho. Balaam blesses instead of cursing, Moses gives the words of Deuteronomy, and from Mount Nebo he sees the promised land before he dies.
2: The starting point. After Moses’ death the LORD tells Joshua, “Be strong and of a good courage.” Two spies are sent from Shittim to Jericho.

The Jordan stops flowing while Israel crosses on dry ground. At Gilgal they set up twelve stones, are circumcised and keep the Passover, and the manna stops. Gilgal is Israel’s base camp for the campaigns.
Israel marches around the city for seven days. On the seventh day the people shout, the walls fall down flat, and Rahab and her family are spared.

ai.m: Probably et-Tell or Khirbet el-Maqatir, West Bank (debated)

2: The first attack fails because of Achan’s sin. After Achan is judged, Israel takes Ai with an ambush.
The Gibeonites trick Israel into a treaty. When five Amorite kings attack Gibeon, Joshua marches all night from Gilgal, and the sun stands still while Israel wins the battle.
Joshua pursues the five kings by Beth-horon, Azekah and Makkedah, then takes Libnah, Lachish, Eglon, Hebron and Debir: the southern campaign.
Jabin king of Hazor gathers the northern kings at the waters of Merom. Israel defeats them, and Joshua burns Hazor, “the head of all those kingdoms”.
The tabernacle is set up at Shiloh, and the remaining land is divided among the tribes by lot.

3: Capital of the northern kingdom, Israel. After a three-year siege it falls to Assyria in 722 BC, and the people are deported because they had turned from the LORD.

0: Mount Moriah. God tests Abraham: “Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac … and offer him there for a burnt offering.” God provides a ram instead, and Abraham names the place “The LORD will provide.” Solomon later builds the temple on Mount Moriah.
3: Babylon takes Jerusalem in three waves: Daniel and others in 605 BC, King Jehoiachin and Ezekiel in 597 BC, and in 586 BC the city and Solomon’s temple are burned and most of the people taken to Babylon.
4: The exiles rebuild the altar and lay the temple’s foundation. The second temple is finished in 516 BC, encouraged by Haggai and Zechariah. Ezra teaches the law, and Nehemiah rebuilds the walls in 52 days.

3: Nebuchadnezzar’s headquarters. Captured King Zedekiah is brought here; his sons are killed before his eyes, then he is blinded and taken to Babylon.

carchemish.m: Karkamış, Türkiye, on the Syrian border

3: In 605 BC Nebuchadnezzar defeats Egypt here, making Babylon master of Judah. The same year the first exiles, including Daniel, are taken.
The king of Assyria places the exiles of Israel “in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes”.
Capital of the Assyrian empire, which carried the northern tribes into exile. Jonah preached here; Nahum foretold its fall, which came in 612 BC.

0: Abram’s family travelled up the Euphrates from Ur towards Haran, passing through the region later ruled from Babylon (Shinar, Genesis 11:2).
3: The exiles settle by the rivers of Babylon (Psalm 137). Daniel serves at the royal court, Ezekiel prophesies by the river Chebar, and Jeremiah writes telling the exiles to seek the peace of the city.
4: In 539 BC Babylon falls to Cyrus of Persia. In 538 BC his decree lets the Jews return. About 50,000 go back under Zerubbabel, and Ezra leads another group in 458 BC.

3: Persian royal city. Daniel sees a vision here, and Esther becomes queen and saves her people.
4: Nehemiah, cupbearer to King Artaxerxes, hears of Jerusalem’s broken walls and is sent to rebuild them in 445 BC.
